he2026recon: Multimodal jailbreak attacks against vision-language models now exploit visual perturbations, yet defenses ignore visual threats, lack attack-specific specificity, and block benign inputs because they have no dedicated detector. ReCon is a black-box defense that pairs a diffusion-based image purifier to neutralize visual perturbations with an autoencoder-based anomaly detector. Its core Reverse Safety Concept Injection maps detected unsafe concepts to fine-grained constructive safe concepts and generates targeted prompts that rectify the attack semantics. Experiments show it raises robustness against jailbreaks while preserving accuracy on benign tasks.
jiang2026sqlagent: Text-to-SQL fails to generalize across databases because SQL reasoning depends on each schema's unique tables, ambiguous semantics, and join paths. SQLAgent decouples exploration from generation. In an exploration stage, it navigates the schema with a Monte Carlo Tree Search-inspired strategy and builds a database-specific knowledge base of triplets linking schema fragments, executable queries, and natural-language descriptions. At deployment, a dual-agent system retrieves relevant knowledge as in-context examples and iteratively generates SQL for user questions. On large text-to-SQL benchmarks it substantially outperforms strong baselines, generalizing to unseen databases through proactive exploration.
li2024control: Prompt-based control is attractive for lexically constrained generation, but language models struggle to impose required words reliably. Systematic evaluation identifies three failures: position bias, where models satisfy constraints only at certain input positions; insensitivity to decoding parameters; and trouble with complex constraints such as compound words. A divide-and-conquer generation strategy splits constraints into smaller ones and is effective for both white-box and black-box models, raising success by over 90 percent on the hardest lexical-constrained task. The analysis clarifies when prompt control works and offers a practical route to customizable generation.
li2024think: Instruction-tuned models summarize English well but do poorly on low-resource language cross-lingual summarization even in few-shot settings. A four-step zero-shot pipeline, SITR, summarizes the source, improves the summary, translates it, and refines the translation, each step with a tailored prompt. Tested with multiple LLMs on two cross-lingual summarization benchmarks across low-resource target languages, the method lets GPT-3.5 and GPT-4 consistently and significantly outperform baselines, showing that low-resource cross-lingual summarization is achievable for large models without task-specific training data.
li2025drs: When readers meet unfamiliar concepts they ask questions the text cannot answer, and models can flag such questions but struggle to help reformulate them. DRS is a zero-shot method that combines an LLM with a depth-first search algorithm to iteratively explore combinations of candidate entities and constrain outputs to those entities, producing structured reformulations that draw out the needed information. The method raises reformulation accuracy for GPT-3.5 from 23.03 to 70.42 percent and for open-source Gemma 2-9B from 26.35 to 56.75 percent, showing how structured search turns weak model reformulation into a usable reading assistant.
li2025metal: Chart generation requires both visual design sense and precise code, which direct VLM prompting cannot combine. METAL decomposes the task into collaborating specialized agents that iteratively design and produce chart code satisfying desired text, layout, color, and type properties. It improves F1 by 5.2 percent over the previous best chart-generation result and by 11.33 percent over direct prompting with Llama 3.2-11B. The framework also exhibits test-time scaling: performance rises monotonically with the log of compute budget, from 29 to 213 tokens, showing that agentic collaboration trades extra inference for better charts.
li2025semvink: Vision-language models cannot detect hidden text or objects in optical illusions unless they perceptually adjust like humans. HC-Bench, 112 images with hidden content, shows leading VLMs near zero accuracy, 0 to 5.36 percent, even with explicit prompts, because they overrely on high-level semantics. Simply downscaling images to 32 to 128 pixels removes redundant visual noise and, surprisingly, unlocks over 99 percent accuracy. The result exposes an architectural bias toward abstract reasoning over low-level visual operations and argues for multi-scale hybrid models for medical imaging, security, and related tasks.
li2025text: VLMs seem like natural tools for recognizing fonts in magazines, papers, and branding, but their fine-grained visual ability is untested. The Font Recognition Benchmark contains 15 common fonts in an easy version with sentences in different fonts and a hard version where each sample renders the names of all 15 fonts, creating a Stroop effect. Evaluations across VLMs find weak font recognition easily disrupted by textual Stroop cues, little benefit from few-shot or chain-of-thought prompting, and attention analysis revealing an inability to capture semantic typographic features.
li2025vertical: Vertical text appears in math and word puzzles, and prior work showed encoder models break when words are aligned vertically, but decoder LLMs were untested. Across text-classification datasets, vertical input sharply degrades accuracy, even though humans read it easily, raising a bypass risk for content filters. Chain-of-thought reasoning does not mitigate the drop, whereas carefully analyzed few-shot examples do. Analysis of tokenization and attention matrices traces the vulnerability to how vertical formatting fragments tokens and disrupts attention, showing that formatting perturbations remain a security concern for modern decoder models.
li2026echofoley: Video-to-audio generation suffers from visual dominance over text, lacks fine-grained controllability, and follows only brief categorical tags. EchoFoley defines a new task for video-grounded sound generation with event-level local control and hierarchical semantics, using a symbolic representation that specifies when, what, and how each sound occurs so that models can generate, insert, or edit sounds. An expert-curated dataset, EchoFoley-6k, provides over 6,000 video-instruction-annotation triplets and 42,000 event annotations. The EchoVidia agentic framework with slow-fast thinking beats recent video-to-audio models by 40.7 percent in controllability and 12.5 percent in perceptual quality.
li2026stdr: 3D Gaussian Splatting renders dynamic scenes in real time, but canonical Gaussians built by aggregating all frames mix space and time, causing incoherence during initialization and poor motion modeling. STDR is a plug-and-play module that learns spatio-temporal distributions per Gaussian: a spatio-temporal mask separates static and dynamic regions, a separated deformation field handles motion, and consistency regularization keeps the two coherent. Added to existing 3DGS dynamic frameworks, it improves reconstruction quality and spatio-temporal consistency on both synthetic and real-world benchmarks without redesigning the base method.
liang2020revisiting: Citywide crowd-flow analytics models inflow and outflow per region from raster data, and CNNs are standard for spatial modeling, yet they learn global dependencies poorly and ignore that regions serve different functions. DeepLGR combines a local feature extractor per region, a global context module that captures global priors and upsamples them back to the grid, and a region-specific predictor based on tensor decomposition that gives each region a customized, parameter-efficient head. On two typical crowd-flow tasks it shows better effectiveness, stability, and generality than prior CNN models.
